{{Short description|Romanian mathematician (1844–1926)}}
[[File:Constantin Climescu.jpg|thumb|Constantin Climescu]]
'''Constantin Climescu''' (30 November 1844 – 6 August 1926) was a [[Moldavia]]n, later [[Romania]]n mathematician and politician.

Born in [[Bacău]], he attended the princely academy in [[Iași]], followed by the sciences faculty of [[Iași University]]. He then left for the [[École Normale Supérieure]] in Paris, and in 1870, took his undergraduate degree from the [[University of Paris]], in mathematics and physical sciences. He was a professor of [[analytic geometry]] and [[spherical trigonometry]] at Iași University from 1871 to 1909, served as dean of the sciences faculty from 1880 to 1901,<ref name="ieseni"/> and as rector of the university from 1901 to 1907.<ref name="b">{{in lang|ro}} Temistocle Bîrsan, [http://www.recreatiimatematice.ro/arhiva/miscelannea/RM12011CLIMESCU.pdf "Restaurarea mormântului lui C. Climescu, fost rector al Universității din Iași"], in ''Recreații Matematice'', nr.1/2011, pp. 3-4</ref>

Meanwhile, from 1884 to 1896, he taught at the upper normal school of Iași, and was among the founders of ''[[Recreații Științifice]]'' periodical in 1883;<ref name="ieseni"/> its chief contributor, he wrote articles on arithmetic, elementary and analytical geometry, algebra and mathematical analysis.<ref name="b"/> He also belonged to the editorial board of ''[[Gazeta Matematică]]'', where he wrote on the historiography of mathematics. He wrote several textbooks that were widely used at the time, on algebra (1887), rational-number arithmetic (1890), elementary geometry (1891) and analytic geometry (1898);<ref name="ieseni"/> the last volume was the second of its type to appear in Romania.<ref name="b"/> He was elected a corresponding member of the [[Romanian Academy]] in 1892.<ref name="ieseni">{{in lang|ro}} Ciprian Teodorescu, [http://bjiasi.ro/wp-content/uploads/2014/01/ACADEMICIENI-IESENI.pdf ''Academicieni ieșeni''], p. 91, at the Gheorghe Asachi Iași County library site</ref>

A member of the [[National Liberal Party (Romania, 1875)|National Liberal Party]], he was elected to the [[Romanian Chamber of Deputies|Assembly of Deputies]] for Bacău [[1884 Romanian general election|in 1884]], and represented Iași in the [[Romanian Senate|Senate]] from 1889 to 1910.<ref name="b"/><ref>[[Constantin Bacalbașa]], ''Bucureștii de altădată (1884-1888)'', pp. 159-60. Bucharest, Editura Humanitas, 2014, {{ISBN|978-973-504-680-4}}</ref> He was an officer of the [[Order of the Star of Romania]], and a commander of the [[Order of the Crown (Romania)|Order of the Crown]].<ref name="b"/> He left the university when he reached the retirement age in 1909, died in 1926 and was buried in [[Eternitatea cemetery]].<ref name="b"/>
